analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata, including three submodule pin changes. EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift:249-250 now passes stopStringScope into the SDK request; EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift:14-31 replays that scope through StopHoldback when reporting the matched stop. The unscoped earliest-match algorithm remains unchanged. The documentation change at docs/architecture/inference.md:1846 describes GPT-OSS matching only Harmony final messages, excluding analysis and tool frames. The supplied documentation excerpts at 2425-2954 are unchanged surrounding context, not evidence of new media, cache, tool or admission controls.
No concrete security regression is established by the visible provider changes. They do not visibly alter authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or cache-scope plumbing. Relevant integration concerns are A-001/TB-007 output-channel integrity, TB-002 relay behavior and T-041 cache isolation; the coordinator remains the trusted plaintext relay.
Material coverage limits remain: libs/mlx, libs/mlx-swift and libs/mlx-swift-lm contain only changed commit pointers, not their implementation diffs. Integration must examine those deltas and the new CBv2StopStringScope/StopHoldback contract, especially whether scan.text preserves an exact raw-prefix scalar count as assumed at StopSequence.swift:30, whether incremental generation and whole-text replay agree across split Harmony markers, and whether bridge scope selection reaches the actual engine stop matcher. Verify that scoped stopping preserves channel filtering, token accounting, bounded generation and cache compatibility. These are unverified contracts, not observed missing controls; this source pass cannot clear the dependency changes.
